notes_on_text: The chapters have no titles, only summaries. The entries of the contents give a short title of the editor’s for each chapter, taken from its summary; the summaries are printed in full at the head of each chapter.
The book does not say in which years the author was in New Zealand.
summary: A young Englishman lands at Auckland with threepence in his pocket and works his way around New Zealand. He is by turns a farm hand, a tramp on the roads of the North Island, a worker on a cattle station, a gum-digger in the kauri gum-fields of the north, and a bushman felling timber, and he is out of money for a time in Wellington.

Along the way he describes Auckland, the hot springs and geysers of Rotorua, Napier, Christchurch, Dunedin, and the southern lakes, and the people he works and travels with. He stays with Maori families, goes to a tangi (a funeral gathering), and writes at length about Maori life. The book is light in tone, with much dialogue; the author says in his introduction that it is no guide to the country.
